body.statement: In the binary one-stratum submodel with \(\mathcal H=\{0\}\), \(b=(1/2,1/2)\), and scalar \(V\in(v_{\min},v_{\max})\), let \(q_{1-\alpha}(V)\) be the right \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(S(0,Z_V)\). There exist \(c_1,c_2,s_0>0\) such that \(c_1s\le q_{1-\alpha}(V)-q_{1-\alpha}(V-s)\le c_2s\) for \(0<s<s_0\). Hence a localized plug-in calibration that may underestimate \(V\) by \(s\) cannot be made uniformly honest with \(o(s)\) critical-value inflation.
body.justification: The result certifies the order of the covariance component when a user replaces the robust spectral envelope by localized plug-in calibration.
body.gap: CCK compares maxima under covariance perturbations, and Fang--Ridder--Xie links covariance to fixed-weight regret; neither gives the sharp quantile sensitivity of this nonlinear path supremum.
body.consumer: Implementers learn when the robust envelope can be localized and how much critical-value inflation a covariance undershoot necessarily costs.
